newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's "repo men" see record bankruptcy year.
newsitem.headline: Germany's "repo men" see record bankruptcy year.

text.p: Germany's Inkasso Federation, the association of repossesion agencies, on Wednesday predicted 1996 would be a record year for bankruptcies.
The "repo men" said they expected 26,400 German firms to go bust this year, up from 22,344, an increase of 18 percent.
"There is no end in sight to this wave of bankruptcies," association vice president Gerti Hoenings told reporters in Berlin.

Commenting on the results of a survey of Inkasso's 350 member organisations, she said unemployment was also driving more and more individuals into the red. People were increasingly holding back payments on bills or paying late.
Personal debt would rise 10 percent this year from 400 billion marks last year, she said, adding that more than two million German households were over-indebted and insolvent.
